solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Having split, flies very quickly

parts.note: something that has split is now in two pieces
the sheep tick or ked is in fact a wingless fly, so ticks can be called flies

explanation.surface: Something breaks apart and the pieces fly off at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a tick is a moment, so doing a thing in a couple of them means doing it almost at once.

clue.text: Long hold-up — hours wasted

indicators.note: wasted here means lost or thrown away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a hitch is a snag that holds things up

explanation.surface: A long delay in which hours are wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective for the hold-up, but it is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to have an urge or craving for it, the verb sense of itching to do it.

clue.text: In experiment I saw sections from original Star Wars?

indicators.note: In tells us the experiment word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to try something is to experiment with it
a log is a section sawn from a tree, so to saw timber is to log it

explanation.surface: Someone describes watching the first Star Wars films as a kind of experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The original Star Wars films came as a set of three, and such a set of works is this word's meaning.

clue.text: Presumably no longer taken with music fan out to lunch?

definitions.text: Presumably no longer taken with music fan
definitions.meaning: read literally: no longer keen on a rock fan, someone who has gone off a rocker
slang for crazy or not all there

explanation.surface: A former music lover who has lost interest and seems absent-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings point to the idiom for being mad: literally gone off a rock enthusiast, and figuratively out to lunch.

clue.text: Taken in by local native

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the two pieces side by side

parts.note: in Britain the local is your neighbourhood pub, an inn
food taken in has been eaten: ate

explanation.surface: A native of the area is fooled by a local.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is everyday British for the nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Native as in inborn: a native talent is one you were born with.

clue.text: Spooner's job to visit Orkneys town

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words have their first sounds exchanged

parts.note: a job is work
to call on someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A job involves a trip to a town in the Orkney Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap is by sound: the W of the first word and the hard C of the second change places.
explanation.definitionFit: The main town and port of the Orkney Islands off the north of Scotland.

clue.text: Vegetable that's small and sweet

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
in Britain a pud (pudding) is the sweet course

explanation.surface: Describing a vegetable that is small and sweet, like a baby carrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' is the British word for dessert, here shortened to PUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is informal for a potato, the most common vegetable.

clue.text: Girl to serve as old maid?

parts.note: Pru is a girl's name, short for Prudence
to dish up food is to serve it

explanation.surface: A girl is asked to wait on table as an elderly housemaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old maid' looks like a servant, fitting 'serve', but means a spinster stereotyped as prim.
explanation.definitionFit: The stereotypical spinster is easily shocked and prim about sex, so behaving like one is being prim.

clue.text: Work as a magician?

definitions.meaning: to work is to succeed or be effective
a magician performs tricks, so working as one means performing one

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job as a stage conjuror.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be effective, and literally describes a conjuror performing an illusion.

clue.text: Greeting, very loud, in deception that one can see through?

indicators.note: in places the greeting and the loud marking inside the deception word

parts.note: a con is a deception or swindle
hi is a greeting
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A loud hello as part of a deception that is easy to see through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One can see through' suggests a transparent trick; it is in fact sheer fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a thin, sheer silk or nylon fabric, so light that it is see-through.

clue.text: Reckoning further cure not working

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Counting again because a medical cure has not worked.
explanation.definitionFit: A second tally of votes or figures is another round of reckoning.

clue.text: Problem I had raised in renting vehicles in Welsh region once

indicators.note: in puts the turned-round pieces inside the renting phrase

parts.note: renting vehicles is car hire

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a snag is a problem
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A traveller reports trouble with a hire car somewhere in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'raised' reads the problem-and-I-had pair upwards, i.e. backwards; Cardiganshire was replaced by Ceredigion in 1974.
explanation.definitionFit: A former county of west Wales, abolished in 1974 and now called Ceredigion.

clue.text: Ancient structure to drag into tour of all bases

indicators.note: into puts the dragging word inside the bases word

parts.note: in rounders, a British bat-and-ball game like baseball, a rounder is scored by running round all the bases
to tow is to drag

explanation.surface: Someone is pulled round a historic site on a guided tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British school game like baseball; a rounder is one full circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall narrow medieval stone tower of the kind found at Irish monastic sites.

clue.text: Old-fashioned message that's dispatched with passion

indicators.note: dispatched means sent off or got rid of, so that letter goes

parts.note: a wire is a telegram, an old way of sending a message

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned telegram sent in a fit of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatched' suggests sending the message, but it removes the W.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger, a fierce passion.

clue.text: Yet needing to be with one that's so described?

definitions.text: Yet needing to be with one that's so described?

parts.words: Yet needing to be with one that's so described?
parts.note: add one (I) to the word yet and you get the yeti, the Himalayan creature whose popular name gives the adjective

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about something that still needs company.
explanation.walkthrough: The yeti is known as the Abominable Snowman, so the adjective is how it is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective in the yeti's nickname, the Abominable Snowman.

clue.text: Old Yankee taken in by slip of a youth

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside the slip word

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake or slip
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An old American fooled by a mere slip of a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip of a youth' reads as one phrase; 'slip' is the British slang BISH, a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what is like or typical of a young lad.

clue.text: Outspoken person responsible for dispatch rider in winter?

indicators.note: outspoken means said aloud, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: to dispatch someone is to kill them, so the one responsible is a slayer

explanation.surface: A blunt person in charge of sending out a winter courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' suggests sending; here it means killing.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical coinage for someone travelling by sleigh, as in snowy winters.

clue.text: UN etc voting on energy solutions

indicators.note: in a down entry on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
E is the physics symbol for energy
fixes are solutions to problems

explanation.surface: The United Nations voting on solutions to the energy problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'UN' looks like the United Nations but is the prefix as in undo.
explanation.definitionFit: Un-, re-, pre- and so on are prefixes, word beginnings that attach to others.

clue.text: State of antagonism ultimately leaves a bitter taste with one

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word antagonism

parts.note: something that leaves a bitter taste is sour
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A state of hostility that leaves a bad taste in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state, named after the river.

clue.text: Starts on shirts and blouses on wash day

indicators.note: starts on asks for the opening letters of the next three words

parts.note: to have a bath is to wash

explanation.surface: Laundry day, beginning with shirts and blouses.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekly holy day of rest, Saturday for Jews and Sunday for many Christians.

clue.text: Female, a reliable sort, endlessly felt for one

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a brick is a dependable, good-hearted person

explanation.surface: A woman, dependable to a fault, who feels for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' reads as a verb; it is the woollen material.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is an example of cloth, a material made by matting wool fibres.

clue.text: Rake fetching in large gold coin cylinder

indicators.note: fetching in means bringing inside, so the large letter goes into the rake word

parts.note: a roue is a rake, a dissolute man
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A croupier's rake gathers in a big pile of gold coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' suggests the casino tool, but it is the libertine.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll of coins wrapped in paper, a tidy cylinder of money.

clue.text: One in hand — or 3 short

indicators.note: short means the final letter is lost

parts.note: 3 points to entry 3-down, meaning crazy, for which bananas is a slang synonym

explanation.surface: A bridge player's lament: one card in hand, three short.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunch of bananas is called a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunch of bananas is called a hand, so each fruit is one in the hand.

clue.text: Money-grubbing to hold back such a tip?

indicators.note: back means those letters are read in reverse
to hold means the clue word contains the letters

explanation.surface: A greedy person reluctant to hand over a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests a gratuity, fitting 'Money-grubbing', but it is the point of a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The writing point of a pen is called its tip.

clue.text: Use a fake King and Queen to move like Castle?

indicators.note: to move means the letters are moved into a new order

parts.words: Use a fake King and Queen
parts.note: the words use a fake are taken as written, with K and Q, the chess abbreviations for king and queen

explanation.surface: Instructions for cheating at chess by using a dodgy king and queen to castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Castle' suggests the chess move but is The Castle, a novel by Franz Kafka.
explanation.definitionFit: Kafka's novel The Castle is nightmarishly bureaucratic, the very model of the adjective.

clue.text: Time to visit for example?

indicators.note: to visit means going into, so the time letter goes inside

parts.note: say is used to introduce an example

explanation.surface: Suggesting a good time to pay someone a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A visit is a period spent somewhere, the length of time you remain as a guest.

clue.text: Exit bar after upsetting female

indicators.note: after upsetting means once these letters have been knocked into disorder

explanation.surface: A woman storms out of a pub after an upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, as in Beatrix Potter, so an example of a female.

clue.text: Version of Bible that is most zealous

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
id est is Latin for that is (i.e.)

explanation.surface: A translation of scripture said to be the most fervent.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen or eager, so the superlative means keenest.

clue.text: A reminder that prejudice holds in Romeo and Juliet

definitions.meaning: something that recalls an earlier thing, like a faint repetition

definitions.text: that prejudice holds in Romeo and Juliet
definitions.meaning: Romeo and Juliet are the NATO alphabet words for R and J; in the word prejudice these two letters hold E, whose NATO word is wanted

explanation.surface: Feuding prejudice runs through the tragedy of Romeo and Juliet as a reminder.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet are the NATO alphabet's R and J; in 'prejudice' they sit either side of E.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint repetition that calls something to mind, and E in the NATO phonetic alphabet.

clue.text: What we should have done perhaps with car tax once

parts.note: an estate is a British estate car, a station wagon

parts.words: What we should have done perhaps
parts.note: a duty is what we ought to do

explanation.surface: A grumble about the old road tax on cars we should have paid.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A former UK tax on a dead person's property, replaced by inheritance tax.
